What did Greek Immigrants in Toronto do in response to Greece's military dictatorship from 1967 to 1974? 

Tagged: Arts

Share this:

  • Twitter
  • LinkedIn

The Greek community in Toronto was one of the largest Greek communities outside of Greece during Greece's military dictatorship from 1967 to 1974. Many community members were deeply affected by the political situation in Greece and organized to protest the dictatorship and support those affected by it.

Some of the actions taken by Greek immigrants in Toronto in response to the military dictatorship include:

1. Protests: Members of the Greek community in Toronto organized protests against the dictatorship, supporting democracy in Greece. These protests included rallies, marches, and demonstrations in public spaces throughout the city.

2. Fundraising: The Greek community in Toronto also organized fundraising efforts to support those affected by the dictatorship in Greece. They raised money to provide financial assistance to political prisoners, exiles, and their families.

3. Cultural activities: Many members of the Greek community in Toronto organized cultural activities to raise awareness about the situation in Greece and to support the democratic resistance movement there. These activities included concerts, film screenings, and theatrical performances.

4. Political lobbying: Members of the Greek community in Toronto also engaged in political lobbying to raise awareness about the situation in Greece and pressure the Canadian government to support democracy in Greece.

Overall, the Greek community in Toronto played an active and crucial role in supporting the democratic resistance movement in Greece during the period of the military dictatorship. Their efforts helped to raise awareness about the situation in Greece and to support those affected by the dictatorship.
